items.t: Zoning (Langley City): The City's Official Community Plan was adopted November 22, 2021.

SSMUH position (Langley City): The City amended its Zoning Bylaw to permit small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots by Bylaw No. 3284, adopted June 17, 2024 — RS1/RS2 permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Bylaw 3284 is the City's own SSMUH bylaw; the Township's Bylaw 6020 does not apply inside the City. Duplexes are the baseline form under that framework.

A secondary suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building; the registered owner must reside on the lot (s.2.4); at least one extra off-street parking space is required; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry. The lesser-of-100 m²/40% figure is Langley City's own rule — never borrowed for another city, and no other city's cap is borrowed here. A listing's "legal suite" claim is a claim to verify against this rule.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: streets and boundaries

items.t: The City of Langley is its own municipality — 10 square kilometres, surrounded by the Township of Langley on the north, east and south and by Surrey's Cloverdale across 196 Street to the west — and nothing on a Township page governs a City lot.

The City's own history in two sentences: the settlement began as "Innes Corners," later "Langley Prairie," a business and service centre on (Old) Yale Road drawing trade from the whole region; on March 15, 1955 the City of Langley incorporated as a separate municipality from the Township.

The diagonal is the giveaway: Fraser Highway cuts across the street grid from Cloverdale to the downtown core at Glover Road and Logan Avenue, while the Langley Bypass (Highway 10) forms the southern commercial edge above the Nicomekl River floodplain.
The City names six neighbourhoods by elementary catchment: Nicomekl, Douglas, Simonds, Blacklock, Alice Brown and Uplands.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: the housing stock

items.t: Most City households live in attached homes: the City is about 80% apartments and townhouses by household, with the detached stock concentrated in the Uplands and the streets north of Grade Crescent and south of the Nicomekl floodplain.

The Official Community Plan (OCP) sorts the stock by form: high-density mixed-use in the "Core" around the planned SkyTrain stations near 196 Street and 203 Street, mid-rise to 12 storeys, low-rise to 6 storeys, townhouses along future frequent bus routes, and compact lots with secondary or garden suites north of Grade Crescent.

Infill here is old for the region: townhouses and 'plexes have sat inside the detached neighbourhoods for decades, including along 203 Street, 50 Avenue and the west side of City Park — a City-acknowledged pattern, not a new experiment.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The plan is the Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3200, adopted November 2021 and read here in its February 2026 consolidation; its Appendix A is a separate Nicomekl River District Neighbourhood Plan for the floodplain-edge lands.

Small-scale multi-unit housing runs through a dedicated zone: the Residential Small Scale Multi Unit Housing (R-SSMUH) zone permits a single dwelling, duplex or townhouse as principal uses, plus a secondary suite and an accessory dwelling unit, to a maximum of four dwelling units per lot, with a 300 square metre minimum lot for a single dwelling, 60% maximum lot coverage and an 11.0 metre principal-building height limit. Zoning.pdf

Density near the stations is a floor, not just a ceiling: the OCP requires minimum site densities of approximately 3.0 floor area ratio (FAR) within the Transit-Oriented Core areas around the planned SkyTrain stations near 196 Street and 203 Street.

Floodplain rule: the Nicomekl River floodplain crosses the city's south side — the City counts the floodplain itself among its 346 acres of parkland — and lots between 56 Avenue and the river sit in the OCP's floodplain and Nicomekl River District framework rather than ordinary residential policy.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Water is metered and billed once a year for most homes: the City reads residential water meters annually in March and puts the charge on the June tax notice; high-volume users are billed every two months instead.
Sewer is not a flat guess — it is calculated at 80% of your metered water consumption, so a leaking toilet or heavy irrigation shows up in the sewer line too.

Douglas Park, at Douglas Crescent and 206 Street, is the civic living room: the City's main events park with a permanent stage, the Douglas Recreation Centre, sports box and water park — and Douglas Park Community School (5409 206 Street) sits in the same park block.

The "downtown" a buyer pictures is one intersection deep: the historic core is the one-way Fraser Highway strip through Innes Corners at Glover Road, and the Langley Centre bus exchange sits at Logan Avenue and Glover Road.

City Park, on the west side, already carries townhouse and 'plex infill on its edge — the OCP's own examples of missing-middle housing in this city are on 201A Street near Sendall Gardens and the west side of City Park.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: development and new projects

items.t: Surrey Langley SkyTrain, King George Station (Surrey) to 203 Street (Langley City), Province of British Columbia with TransLink: 16-kilometre elevated Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway with eight stations, ending at the Langley City Centre terminus at 203 Street and Industrial Avenue in the City — status: major construction under way, with guideway installation, pile driving on Industrial Avenue and station construction listed in the project's fall 2026 notices (as of November 3, 2026).

SkyTrain power supply, Fraser Highway between 140 Street (Surrey) and 203 Street (Langley City), BC Hydro: overhead line relocation largely complete and energization work running spring 2026 to late 2027, fed from the Fleetwood (Surrey) and McLellan (Langley) substations — status: under construction (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's published 2026 property tax summary sets Class 1 Residential at a total of $4.2067 per $1,000 of taxable value, of which the City of Langley general municipal portion is $2.5937 per $1,000, with the balance to Metro Vancouver (shown as GVRD), school, TransLink (GVTA), BC Assessment and the Municipal Finance Authority.

Water for 2026 is $2.06 per cubic metre plus a $75 annual fee, metered; sewer is charged on 80% of water consumption at $2.41 per cubic metre plus a $75 fee; the 2026 single-family solid waste charge is $432.

The City's 2026–2030 Financial Plan bylaw (Bylaw No. 3318) context: about 75% of operating spending is funded through property taxes and utility charges billed at the end of May each year, and the draft plan balanced on a 3.57% property tax increase — context for the rate above, not a second rate.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: getting around

items.t: The bus hub is Langley Centre exchange at Logan Avenue and Glover Road downtown; its anchor route is TransLink Route 503 Fraser Highway Express, running Surrey Central Station to Aldergrove via Langley Centre on Fraser Highway, with the Surrey Central–Langley Centre segment in the Frequent Transit Network.

Until the SkyTrain opens, rail access is by bus: Langley Centre routes connect to Surrey Central and King George stations on the Expo Line, and Route 595 runs from Langley Centre to Maple Meadows Station for the West Coast Express corridor.

By road, the city is crossed by Fraser Highway (to Surrey and Aldergrove), 200 Street (to Willowbrook and Highway 1) and the Langley Bypass, Highway 10 (to Cloverdale and Delta); Highway 1 itself runs through the Township north of the city, not through the City.

blocks.text: City of Langley Homes for Sale: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the station-area rules before pricing a lot on potential: within the Transit-Oriented Core around 196 Street and 203 Street, the OCP sets a minimum density of about 3.0 FAR, which cuts both ways — it supports assembly value and constrains a low-density rebuild.

Construction exposure is a current, dated risk: the SkyTrain project's weekly advisories list single-lane traffic in effect 24/7 along most of the Fraser Highway corridor with pedestrian and cyclist detours — a Fraser Highway or Industrial Avenue purchase closes into an active construction zone.

items.t: Source: langleycity.ca

faq.q: Is the City of Langley the same as the Township for duplex rules?
faq.a: No — separate municipalities, separate bylaws. Inside the City: Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 (number only), SSMUH Bylaw 3284, suite = lesser of 100 m² / 40% with owner-occupancy (s.2.4) and registry recording. The Township's Bylaw 6020 and 120 m² cap do not apply here.

faq.q: Is a "legal suite" in a City listing really legal?
faq.a: Only if it meets Bylaw 3300: Lesser of 100 m² / 40%, owner residing on the lot, inspected and approved through a building permit, and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry.

faq.q: Is this the City or the Township — does it change anything?
faq.a: Yes, everything municipal. The City of Langley is a separate 10-square-kilometre municipality incorporated March 15, 1955; its tax rate, utility charges, zoning bylaw and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3200 are its own, and Township of Langley figures — including its much larger rural tax and utility tables — do not apply to a City address. Check the municipality on the BC Assessment and City tax records, not the postal address, which just says "Langley."

faq.q: Which schools serve a City of Langley home?
faq.a: School District No. 35 (Langley) runs one secondary school inside the city: Langley Secondary at 21405 56 Avenue, Grades 9–12, with H.D. Stafford Middle School as its middle school. The district groups six City elementaries in the Langley Secondary family: Blacklock Fine Arts Elementary (5100 206 Street), Douglas Park Community (5409 206 Street), Nicomekl Elementary (20050 53 Avenue), Simonds Elementary (20190 48 Avenue), Uplands Elementary (4471 207A Street) and Alice Brown Elementary (20011 44 Avenue). Catchment is by address; confirm in the district's locator.

faq.q: How many units can go on a detached lot here?
faq.a: Up to four, in the zone built for it. The R-SSMUH zone allows a maximum of four dwelling units per lot across the permitted forms — a principal dwelling, duplex or townhouse, plus a secondary suite and an accessory dwelling unit as secondary uses — subject to the zone's 300 square metre minimum lot area, 60% coverage cap and 11.0 metre height limit. Whether a specific lot carries that zone is a City zoning-map check. Zoning.pdf

faq.q: When does the SkyTrain actually arrive, and where is the station?
faq.a: It is under construction now, not a proposal. The provincial project site states SkyTrain is coming "between King George Station in Surrey and 203 Street in Langley City," with the Langley City Centre terminus at 203 Street and Industrial Avenue; the project's own construction pages show guideway and station construction under way along Fraser Highway and Industrial Avenue in fall 2026. The in-service date is the project's to state — check the project site for the current target before relying on one.

faq.q: Is the City of Langley the same as the Township of Langley?
faq.a: No — the City of Langley is its own municipality, separate from the Township of Langley, with its own Official Community Plan (adopted November 22, 2021) and its own Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300.

faq.q: How many units can a Langley City single-family lot hold?
faq.a: Under Bylaw No. 3284 (adopted June 17, 2024), RS1 and RS2 lots permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop.
